title: Church and the Poor
definition: Church and the Poor teaches the Church's responsibility to show mercy, generosity, justice, and practical concern for those in need.
summary: Church and the Poor addresses the congregation's responsibility to show mercy, justice, and practical care toward those in need.
christFocus: Jesus Christ identified with the lowly and calls His people to serve the least with love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on the church's posture toward poverty and vulnerability. Scripture does not allow the congregation to honor the wealthy while ignoring the poor. Mercy toward the needy reflects the compassion of Christ and the righteousness of God's kingdom.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because poverty can be invisible to comfortable believers. The Church's witness is damaged when it proclaims grace while despising the needy. This doctrine calls for compassion that is wise, personal, and rooted in the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Learn the needs around and within your church before assuming they are being met. Give, serve, advocate, and befriend with dignity rather than pity. Resist favoritism toward those who can benefit the church socially or financially.
